name: Asset designer help
description: Help mode entries (help@1) for the Asset designer plugin: the page, its toolbar, the envelope fields, the tabs and the settings.
author: Brett

entries.title: Asset designer
entries.text: Design any asset type without code: pick the type, open a saved asset or start a new one, fill in its fields, and save once the validation gate is clean.

entries.title: Asset designer settings
entries.text: The designer's own settings under Settings → Plugins: the type it opens on and whether live preview starts on.

entries.title: Asset type
entries.text: Every asset type the framework registers, grouped. Changing it starts a blank asset of that type.

entries.title: Open
entries.text: The assets you have saved of this type. Pick one to edit it, or New asset to start again.

entries.title: Start from
entries.text: Copies a built-in asset of this type into a new draft so you can change it. The built-in itself is never touched.

entries.title: New
entries.text: Starts a blank asset of the chosen type with every required field at its default.

entries.title: Duplicate
entries.text: Makes a new draft from the current asset under a fresh id; it gets its own identifier when saved.

entries.title: Reload
entries.text: Re-reads the saved assets from the server and registers them into the running console.

entries.title: Delete
entries.text: Removes this saved asset from the designer's data folder. Built-in assets cannot be deleted here.

entries.title: Save
entries.text: Writes the asset as a standard asset@1 file with its designed@1 manifest. Off while the validation gate lists problems; the server validates again before writing.

entries.title: Live preview
entries.text: Puts the draft on the real chrome while it is valid; turning it off puts the previous asset back.

entries.title: Settings interface
entries.text: Opens the settings interface asset of this chrome type (toolbar, tab group, banner, menu), with every one of its tokens as a field.

entries.title: Toolbar settings interface
entries.text: Opens the designer on the settings interface every toolbar's right-click Settings dialog renders through.

entries.title: Tab group settings interface
entries.text: Opens the designer on the settings interface every tab row's right-click Settings dialog renders through.

entries.title: Open the designer
entries.text: Goes to the Asset designer page.

entries.title: Design an asset…
entries.text: Opens the Asset designer from any right-click menu.

entries.title: Design an asset…
entries.text: Opens the Asset designer from any right-click menu.

entries.title: Id
entries.text: The asset's id: 2–48 lowercase letters, digits and dashes. A built-in id is refused on save.

entries.title: Name
entries.text: The name shown in pickers; suggests an id while the asset is new.

entries.title: Version
entries.text: Semantic version; bumped by the designed@1 manifest on every save.

entries.title: Tags
entries.text: Comma-separated tags kept in the asset envelope.

entries.title: Description
entries.text: A sentence on what this asset is for.

entries.title: Fields
entries.text: Every field the asset type registers: chrome settings fields, required fields and optional fields, each with its own control and inline error.

entries.title: JSON
entries.text: The whole data object as JSON for anything the fields do not reach. Apply runs the validation gate.

entries.title: Apply JSON
entries.text: Parses the JSON text into the asset's data and runs the validation gate.

entries.title: Data (JSON)
entries.text: The asset's data object. Edit it here when a field is a list or an object.

entries.title: Preview
entries.text: Draws the asset as its host would; with Live preview on it is also on the real chrome.

entries.title: Manifest
entries.text: The designed@1 manifest a saved asset carries: its identifier (uid), revision, hash and times.

entries.title: Starting asset type
entries.text: The asset type the designer opens on.

steps.say: Pick an asset type, then open a saved asset or start from a built-in one.
Fill in the fields; problems show next to the field they are about, and Save turns on when the asset is clean.
Toolbars, tab groups, banners and menus also have a settings interface asset you can edit here.
